dominant_strengths: Faithful Xcode-like chrome with convincing traffic lights, tab bar, breadcrumb, and status bar—native integration feels earned
Restrained syntax palette (pinks, teals, soft yellows on charcoal) reads cleanly without rainbow noise
Monospaced rhythm and gutter alignment are tight; line numbers, indentation, and selection highlight all line up correctly
dominant_weaknesses: It is essentially a re-skin of Xcode—almost zero original interaction, layout invention, or editorial point of view
Sidebar file icons are flat colored squares; they read as placeholders rather than crafted glyphs and weaken hierarchy
Static screenshot with no indication of motion, cursor, hover, or live affordances—reflective payoff is thin
fix_priorities: Introduce one genuinely original mechanic (inline AI scratchpad, semantic minimap, or context rail) to justify existing
Replace square file icons with proper language glyphs and tighten sidebar typographic scale
Add a visible cursor, selection state, or diagnostic peek to communicate live editor behavior
Differentiate the breadcrumb and tab strip slightly so active file has stronger figure/ground
rationale.norman_balance: Visceral and behavioral both land via Xcode mimicry, but reflective value is low because nothing here is memorably the designer's own.
rationale.intent_fit: It convincingly depicts a code editor, but 'original' is barely satisfied—execution is competent yet derivative.
